choices.content: \(x\) is any real number except \(1\) or \(-1\)

question.prompt: The complete set of \(x\)-values satisfying the inequality \(\dfrac{x^2-4}{x^2-1}\gt0\) is the set of all \(x\) such that:

solutions.explanation:
First exclude \(x=\pm1\), where the denominator is zero. A nonzero quotient is positive exactly when its numerator and denominator have the same sign. This gives two cases.

If both are positive, we need \(x^2>4\) and \(x^2>1\). The stronger condition \(x^2>4\) already guarantees both, giving \(x<-2\) or \(x>2\).

If both are negative, we need \(x^2<4\) and \(x^2<1\). The stronger condition \(x^2<1\) guarantees both, giving \(-1<x<1\).

These two sign cases exhaust all ways the quotient can be positive. The values \(x=\pm2\) make the numerator zero, so strict positivity excludes them; \(x=\pm1\) remain undefined. Therefore the complete set is
\[
\boxed{x<-2\quad\text{or}\quad -1<x<1\quad\text{or}\quad x>2},
\]
choice \(\mathrm A\).
solutions.title: Match numerator and denominator signs
